prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1352; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a sideswipe collision during a lane change on a multi-lane roadway. Insured vehicle contacted the claimant's vehicle on the driver's side rear quarter panel. Both drivers reported to be stopped at the scene. Police report requested. Claimant reports neck and lower back pain and has not yet sought treatment.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed no attorney retained and prefers to handle the claim directly. Claimant describes lower back strain with stiffness and limited range of motion, mainly when sitting for long periods. Advised claimant of the medical documentation needed and the process for submitting bills and records.

Entry 3: Recorded insured's statement. Insured states they checked the mirror and signal before moving into the adjacent lane but did not see the claimant vehicle in the blind spot. Insured accepts that the lane change was the cause of contact. Photos of both vehicles reviewed and consistent with the reported impact point.

Entry 4: Claimant provided initial medical visit notes. Diagnosis listed as acute lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treatment plan includes rest, over-the-counter pain relief, and physical therapy referral. Work restrictions noted for the next two weeks. Injury evaluation is ongoing and reserve set pending further records.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with claimant. Claimant reports pain has improved slightly but still limits lifting and driving for extended periods. Physical therapy scheduled to begin shortly. Liability accepted on insured's side, pending final review of the police report. Claim remains open for injury evaluation and property damage estimate.
